newsitem.title: USA: Merrill's Clough sees Fed easing, bullish on bonds.
newsitem.headline: Merrill's Clough sees Fed easing, bullish on bonds.

text.p: Merrill Lynch Chief Investment Strategist Charles Clough said Friday that he believes the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates later this year because of deflationary pressures in the economy.

"I think the Fed will be easing later in the year," Clough told Reuters after the speech to Boston College donors. "After six years of economic expansion, there's more capacity then we need," he added.
Clough said many sectors of the stock market, including defensive issues, have been overbid and will likely suffer from weaker than expected earnings.
But he did like financial stocks, insurance companies, some airlines, and U.S. treasuries, particularly zero coupon bonds.
In particular, he mentioned Chase Manhattan Corp, Travelers Group Inc and Conseco Inc.
He recommended a portfolio allocation of 55 percent bonds, 40 percent stocks and five percent cash.
"Our sense is that inflationary fears that are built into bonds right now are going to ease a bit," he said. "If the stock market falls here we might scare some consumption," he added.

He said the economy is threatened by sated consumers burdened by high debt levels and weakening auto sales and construction. Companies are warning of lower earnings and are cutting back on backlogs, he added.
Inflation has been "remarkably" absent, and even commodity prices fell after the Fed last month hiked interest rates for the first time in two years.
"The central bank, I think, is fighting the last war. It's fighting an inflationary war," he said.
